title: SE roleplay matrix for latency-obsessions (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight, practice-first roleplay matrix focused on buyers and engineers whose primary buying signal is latency (p50/p95/p99) and tight SLOs. Goal: give SEs a short, repeatable set of cards and scripts to run 10–15 minute drills that surface the true constraint (network, model, infra, prompt design) and map to a Redwood action (hosted route, dedicated reservation, private deploy, or runtime config).

Audience:
- Field SEs and PS engineers pairing with platform/product teams
- Sellers prepping for pilot scoping calls where latency is the gating criterion

How to use this doc:
- Print or open one card per scenario. Run 3 rounds per practice: discovery (4 min), rebuttal + demo script (6 min), close & technical next steps (5 min). Give 2 feedback points: accuracy of diagnosis, clarity of fallback.

Scoring rubric (quick):
- Diagnosis (0–3): Did the SE ask the two key latency provenance questions?
- Intervention (0–3): Did they recommend a correct short-term fallback (model variant, batching off, route to dedicated)?
- Confidence + Commitment (0–2): Clear next step with ownership and metric to measure.
- Total: 0–8; target practice average: >=6 before using live.

Card format (one-per-scenario):
- Persona (who)
- Buying trigger (why now)
- Live metrics they quote (what they care about)
- Seller opening (30s)
- 3 discovery questions (priority order)
- Rapid demo script (what to show in 90s)
- Short rebut/backstop lines (30–60s)
- Recommended Redwood play (immediate + mid-term)
- Fail mode / escalation (when to call SRE or PS)

Scenario A: Edge customer — low p90 for web chat
- Persona: Lead infra engineer at consumer app (single-region)
- Trigger: Users complain about 300–700ms perceived lag on ‘typing’ assist; product team wants <150ms p90 for core funnel
- Quotes: "p95 for short prompts is 480ms, p99 spikes to 1.4s", "we cannot tolerate cold-starts"
- Seller opening: "Quick note — we usually split latency into network + model compute + runtime queuing. Let's walk each quickly so I can recommend the smallest change to get you under 150ms p90."
- Discovery Qs: 1) Typical prompt token length distribution? 2) Traffic pattern (bursts vs steady)? 3) Currently using streaming or batch calls?
- Rapid demo: Show hosted API p90 baseline for a 16-token prompt -> then show switching to a trimmed model variant + streaming + prefix cache enabled (in Console) and the p90 improvement numbers (fake demo metrics, emphasize how to reproduce).
- Rebut lines: "If it's network vs compute we can try regional routing first — pin to nearest region and enable TLS keep-alives. If compute is the blocker you can request a dedicated pool for daytime traffic."
- Redwood play: Immediate: enable streaming + prefix caching + route to nearest region; Mid-term: reserved dedicated pool with autoscale windows for peak times and enable quantized variant for <150ms p90 test runs.
- Fail mode: If p99 still > 800ms after above, escalate to SRE — likely kernel/sequence-length pathological case or customer model modifications needed.

Scenario B: Enterprise platform — p99 SLO and deterministic tails
- Persona: Platform reliability lead at regulated enterprise
- Trigger: SLA requires p99 < 500ms for document summarization microservice (avg length 800 tokens)
- Quotes: "We see long tails when we hit >512 context; sometimes jobs queue for minutes during peak"
- Seller opening: "We treat 'tail latency' as a capacity + model-length problem. Two quick experiments reduce tails: model sharding (serve shorter segments) or offloading to dedicated pools sized for your arrival distribution."
- Discovery Qs: 1) Mean and max context length by endpoint? 2) Are you pinning model versions? 3) Nightly vs daytime arrival skew?
- Rapid demo: Show console plotting per-route latency by sequence length, highlight queuing vs RPS correlated spikes, then flip to canary dedicated capacity sized to observed qps and show tail drop.
- Rebut lines: "If you can break long inputs into chunked summaries and reassemble we often shave tails without extra infra cost. If business can't, dedicated capacity is the predictable path."
- Redwood play: Immediate: set sequence-length-based routing with fallback to a lower-compute variant; Mid-term: plan for reserved capacity with SLA and traffic shaping.
- Fail mode: If dedicated pool still shows spikes, open ticket with Infra/Serving runtime to inspect kernel selection and KV cache behavior.

Scenario C: Cost-constrained startup with strict latency budget
- Persona: CTO of a Seed-stage app optimizing for unit economics
- Trigger: Need 120ms median for replies with token cost ceiling; cannot afford large reserved spend
- Quotes: "We have 200ms median now but tokens cost kills margins"
- Seller opening: "We can approach this two ways: reduce token work per request (prompt engineering, embeddings + retrieval) or change serving profile (micro-batching off, model quantization). Let's prioritize cheap wins."
- Discovery Qs: 1) Are replies dominated by generation or retrieval? 2) How tolerant are you to lower quality that’s 'good enough'? 3) Where is most spend coming from (tokens vs embedding calls)?
- Rapid demo: Show Optimize suggestions (batch/quantization presets) and a quick split test in Console simulating qps with and without KV cache.
- Rebut lines: "Small latency wins often come from caching repeated prefixes and eliminating unnecessary context; try a 2-week A/B with cached prefixes enabled and compare unit cost."
- Redwood play: Immediate: enable KV prefix caching, disable large batch windows for low-latency routes, switch to a quantized variant; Mid-term: configure Optimize suggested quantization and monitor quality regressions via eval set.
- Fail mode: If quality regressions unacceptable, scope a hybrid: hosted low-latency route for critical reads and lower-cost batched route for bulk processing.

Scenario D: Security-sensitive on-prem — NAT/network unpredictability
- Persona: Infra security lead, wants private deployment but worried about network/router latency
- Trigger: Pilot on VPC shows inconsistent p95 due to upstream firewall inspection peaks
- Quotes: "We saw 300ms spikes during scans"
- Seller opening: "Network inspection is often invisible to model serving. We can approach by isolating inference egress, running health probes, and using on-prem collaterals to show deterministic behavior."
- Discovery Qs: 1) Can you carve out a private subnet for inference to skip intrusive proxies? 2) Is there an SNI/TLS inspection layer? 3) What are expected throughput bursts?
- Rapid demo: Show a private deploy blueprint and a synthetic probe run inside customer VPC to reproduce spikes.
- Rebut lines: "If network is the cause, moving to an on-prem package or colocating hardware behind the inspection perimeter is the solution — Redwood can provide a PS-eng kit to run a 48h smoke test."
- Redwood play: Immediate: run smoke probes + network capture with PS; Mid-term: design on-prem package with local routing and dedicated NICs.
- Fail mode: If network still unpredictable, recommend pilot rollback and joint runbook with customer network ops.

Practice workshop outline (30–45m):
- 0–5m: Quick intro to the matrix and scoring rubric
- 5–20m: Round-robin roleplays (3 scenarios, 5m each + 2m feedback)
- 20–30m: Focused coaching on rebut lines and demo checklist for Console toggles
- 30–40m: Rapid live demo rehearsal (SE pairs)
- 40–45m: Capture 2 improvements to the matrix and next practice date

Appendix: Quick console checklist (what to demo in 90s)
- Show per-route latency chart and filter by sequence-length
- Toggle streaming on/off and explain perceived latency differences
- Show model variant switch in Console and run a 5-request p90 probe
- Turn on prefix/KV cache and show perf delta (repro example tokens)
- Demonstrate creating a dedicated pool request (screenshot of form + expected lead time)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Collect real customer metric cutouts from SEs (request anonymized screenshots) to add 6 canonical examples
- Build a small Console quick-run template that automates the 90s demo values (product ask: UX dev ticket: jira:CON-198)
- Add a one-page cheat card for AE to use in discovery calls with checklist and 3-lines rebut (deliverable: 1-pager by Feb 14)

Notes to self: rough phrases for coaching
- "Short prompts: test for cold-start vs kernel-selection — ask for 3 samples"
- "If they only quote median, push to p95/p99 or sample-by-length"
- "Offer A/B pilot with measurement window and define success metric up front"

References and artifacts to attach later:
- Confluence: latency playbook (internal), sample dashboards, prior SE screen recordings (link placeholders above)

End of draft — this is intentionally skeletal and practice-first. Want feedback from Matt (SE lead) and Jamal (PS) on the demo checklist and a small list of real screenshots to make the 90s demo credible in rehearsals.
